page: Microsoft Azure D96lds_v5 is an x86_64 virtual server powered by a 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon 8370C processor hosted on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system provides 96 dedicated vCPUs derived from 48 physical cores with two threads per core. Its cache hierarchy includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory capacity is provisioned at 192.0 GB, establishing a 2.0 GB per vCPU allocation. The hardware configuration includes 3,865 GB of local solid-state drive storage, while operating without discrete graphics acceleration.

Benchmark evaluations indicate substantial multi-core compute capabilities. The instance achieved a Geekbench multi-core score of 17,699.0 and a multi-threaded stress-ng result of 93,258.02, both positioning in the top quartile of tested servers. Extended instruction sets deliver an upper-decile PassMark CPU encryption score of 86,381.58 and Clang software compilation throughput of 55,338.0. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reached 328.17 GB/s. Conversely, single-thread performance benchmarks such as single-core Geekbench (1,711.0) and single-threaded gzip compression register within median ranges.

The 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio represents a compute-dense configuration rather than a memory-expanded one, making the instance less suited for memory-intensive in-memory databases. Instead, the balance of high core counts and 3,865 GB of fast local SSD storage delivers efficient parallel processing for IO-heavy scratch workloads. The server is well aligned for large-scale software compilation, distributed continuous integration jobs, multi-threaded compression or decompression pipelines, and high-throughput web serving.
description: Microsoft Azure D96lds_v5 is a compute-dense virtual machine featuring 96 vCPUs and 48 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz under Microsoft Hyper-V. Built on x86_64 architecture with 48 MB of L3 cache, the system supports AVX-512 and hardware cryptographic instructions. Memory is configured at 192.0 GB, yielding a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio, complemented by 3,865 GB of direct-attached local SSD storage and zero GPUs. Benchmark results demonstrate strong multi-threaded execution, with high Clang compilation throughput, robust memory bandwidth reaching 328.17 GB/s for uncached reads, and top-decile CPU encryption performance. Single-core metrics sit in the median tier. The instance provides efficient hardware scaling for high-concurrency workloads requiring substantial local disk storage, including multi-threaded software builds, batch data transformation, and static web serving.
